about.title: Colusa Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Colusa is a small city, but its roads still carry steady traffic through downtown and out toward Route 20. Public records show six injury collisions and seven injured people in the most recent final year, with reported crashes clustering on Friday afternoons around lunchtime — often near Fremont, Bridge, and Market Streets where local traffic mixes with through-traffic. When a crash happens here, the aftermath can be confusing: unfamiliar insurance forms, medical bills, and calls from an adjuster asking for a statement. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured drivers, passengers, cyclists, and pedestrians in Colusa with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate the crash, handle communication with insurers, and help protect your right to recover compensation. There's no cost to get connected, and any attorney you're matched with works on contingency, meaning fees only come from a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government entity's road or vehicle was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Getting connected early helps preserve your options before deadlines pass.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible, you can still recover a reduced share of damages. An early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to shift more blame onto you, which is why it's worth speaking with an attorney first.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Full Story Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in car accident cases. An independent attorney can help make sure evidence — photos, witness statements, medical records — is gathered before it disappears, so your claim reflects the full impact of the crash.

items.question: Where do most reported crashes happen in Colusa?
items.answer: Public collision records point to higher activity along Route 20, Fremont Street, Bridge Street, and Market Street, with Friday midday hours seeing more reported crashes than other times. This doesn't mean any one spot is unsafe, just that traffic patterns there are worth being aware of.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim, and an independent attorney can help you understand what, if anything, you're required to share.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing — LawProactive is a free service, and there's no obligation to move forward after you're connected. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: What if the crash involved a Colusa County road or government vehicle?
items.answer: Claims involving government entities in California often come with a much shorter deadline, sometimes as little as six months, along with special notice requirements. It's worth getting connected with an attorney quickly if this applies to your situation.
